chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Muawiya ibn Ammar, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
The one in Ihram cannot take (cut) from the hairs of one not in Ihram.

key_terms.الْحَلَالِ: The permissible one / one not in Ihram
key_terms.الْمُحْرِمُ: The person in the state of Ihram (ritual consecration for Hajj or Umrah)

ai.seo_question: Can a person in Ihram cut the hair of someone who is not in Ihram?
ai.summary: This concise hadith from al-Kafi clarifies a specific nuance in the prohibitions of Ihram, establishing that the restriction on cutting hair applies primarily to the individual's own body, thereby permitting the removal of hair from others. In Shia fiqh, this distinction is crucial for understanding the scope of 'taharrum' (prohibitions), ensuring that acts like getting a haircut or shaving by a non-muharrim do not invalidate the pilgrimage status. It reflects the juristic principle that personal prohibitions in Ihram are generally self-referential unless explicitly extended to others.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Muawiya Bin Ammar, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘The one in Ihraam cannot take (cut) from the hairs of one not in Ihraam’.
en.sarwar: 7. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ibn abu ‘Umayr from Mu‘awiyah ibn ‘Ammar who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘
One in the state of Ihram must not cut any hair of al- Hallal (one who is not in the state of Ihram).”’
